text.headline: Frank Rosenblatt
text.text: Frank Rosenblatt introduced the Perceptron, an early hardware and software implementation of a learning network capable of binary classification. It was celebrated as a breakthrough because it could learn from data, though its inability to solve non-linear problems like the XOR function caused major setbacks later.

text.headline: The Perceptrons Critique and AI Winter
text.text: Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published their book Perceptrons, mathematically proving the strict limitations of single-layer networks. This critical analysis drained funding and enthusiasm for neural network research, triggering the first major

text.headline: Introduction of Backpropagation Concepts
text.text: Paul Werbos was the first to propose the backpropagation algorithm for training multi-layer neural networks in his Ph.D. dissertation. Although his work was largely overlooked at the time, it established the mathematical foundation for optimizing deep networks.

text.headline: Popularization of Backpropagation
text.text: Geoffrey Hinton, David Rumelhart, and Ronald Williams popularized the backpropagation algorithm through a landmark paper showing how it efficiently calculates gradients. This breakthrough solved how to train multi-layered networks, breathing new life into the stagnant field of connectionism.

text.headline: Convolutional Networks for Handwritten Digits
text.text: Yann LeCun and his colleagues successfully applied backpropagation to multi-layer convolutional neural networks to read handwritten ZIP codes. This system, known as LeNet, proved the viability of deep learning for practical, real-world computer vision tasks.

text.headline: Invention of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
text.text: Sepp Hochreiter and Jürgen Schmidhuber introduced LSTM networks, a specialized type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). This architecture successfully mitigated the vanishing gradient problem, enabling models to effectively process long sequential data like speech and text.

text.headline: The AlexNet Breakthrough
text.text: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton designed AlexNet, a deep Convolutional Neural Network that crushed the competition in the ImageNet visual recognition challenge. This event is widely credited with igniting the modern deep learning spring and accelerating massive industrial adoption.

text.headline: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
text.text: Ian Goodfellow and his colleagues introduced GANs, a framework where two neural networks—a generator and a discriminator—compete against each other. This adversarial training process revolutionized generative modeling, allowing AI to synthesize remarkably realistic images, audio, and video.

text.headline: The Transformer Architecture
text.text: Ashish Vaswani and his co-authors introduced the Transformer model, replacing traditional recurrence with a self-attention mechanism to process entire data sequences in parallel. This architecture became the foundational backbone for state-of-the-art modern natural language processing and modern generative AI.
